I guess this started about five months ago. At first I thought it was just burnout from the hours, but it’s gone way beyond that. I’m… slow now. Even walking from my desk to the printer feels like wading through mud. I catch myself just staring at my screen, not moving, while emails pile up. My team’s noticed I’m “off,” though no one says it directly.

I cry a lot, which is embarrassing. On the subway, in the bathroom at work, sometimes in my apartment for no obvious reason. It just hits me and I can’t hold it in.

What scares me is what I’ve started to believe about myself. I’m convinced the mistakes I’ve made at work have screwed up deals and hurt people financially, like I’ve ruined retirement funds, families’ lives. I know everyone says that’s not really on me, but it feels like I’m somehow responsible for everything that goes wrong.

A few weeks ago, I collected a bunch of my old prescriptions and some over-the-counter stuff and kept them in a drawer, planning to take them all. I wrote out instructions for my parents about my accounts. I didn’t go through with it, but it wasn’t some abstract thought—it was a plan. This is really affecting my job and I’m barely holding it together.
